High-Level Project Summary

ÓRBITA CERO is an interactive, accessible educational space mission simulator designed for learners aged 8 and up. We developed a bilingual (English/Spanish) web game that transforms complex aerospace engineering and orbital mechanics into intuitive, hands-on gameplay.

The project directly addresses the challenge by allowing students and teams to design, launch, and operate real space missions while managing six core engineering constraints: budget, mass, power, data, communications, and time. It features a 10-chapter narrative campaign, real-time telemetry, and live integration with NASA's DONKI space weather database, which triggers active solar storms within missions. To ensure maximum inclusion, the platform supports mouse, keyboard, and webcam-powered computer-vision hand gestures and body-control flight.

ÓRBITA CERO is important because it bridges arcade accessibility with genuine scientific rigor, inspiring the next generation of space explorers through inclusive, data-driven learning.
details:
What it does & How it works:

ÓRBITA CERO is an interactive, bilingual (English/Spanish) web-based space mission simulator designed for learners aged 8 and older. It bridges arcade accessibility with real aerospace engineering through multiple gamified modes:

  • Profiles & Avatar Customization: Players log in with a custom name and 4-digit PIN to track stars, coins, and explorer ranks. Users can select mission roles (Pilot, Co-Pilot, Engineer, Scientist) and change avatars at any time.
  • Interactive Solar System Hub & AI Guide: An animated solar system serves as the main menu where an alien guide explains controls aloud, shares planetary facts, and guides players. The language toggles instantly between Spanish and English (ES/EN).
  • 10-Level Story Mode (Zuri's Star Map): Players help explorer Zuri and her robot BIT recover 10 shattered star-map fragments across planetary stations—ranging from rocket assembly and ISS module docking to lunar rovers, Mars drones, and exoplanet habitability analysis.
  • Free Mission & Mission Ladder (Real Physics): Teams (1–4 players) manage six real engineering constraints—budget, mass, power, data, communications, and time—across 7 design tabs (Orbit, Launcher, Spacecraft, Science Instruments, Link, and Review). It features live telemetry, stage separation, launch windows, and in-flight anomalies like reaction wheel vibrations.
  • Training Center & Webcam Controls: Includes 6 mini-games (orbital debris cleanup, capsule landing, lunar patrol, galactic memory, and astronaut trivia) plus webcam-powered hand gestures and a 3D Free Flight mode where players spread their arms like wings to steer through crystal worlds.

Benefits & Expected Impact:

  • Educational Impact: Simplifies complex orbital mechanics and mission planning into intuitive gameplay, empowering classrooms and students globally.
  • NASA Data Literacy: Connects users directly to real space weather, making scientific data approachable for children.
  • Accessibility: Eliminates hardware barriers by running in standard browsers with touchless computer-vision controls for diverse learners.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used:

  • Frontend & Game Engine: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and 2D/3D Canvas rendering.
  • Computer Vision & Accessibility: Webcam hand-tracking and body-pose gesture recognition APIs, alongside Web Speech API for voice synthesis.
  • Open Data Integration: Real-time REST API connection to NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information) to fetch solar flares and coronal mass ejections.

Creativity & Team Considerations:

ÓRBITA CERO is uniquely creative because it merges deep scientific accuracy (real planetary parameters, orbital altitudes, and live NASA space weather feeds that trigger in-game solar storms) with whimsical storytelling and zero-touch physical interaction. Our team carefully considered inclusivity (bilingual support, voice narration, hand gestures), educational progression (from guided stories to hard engineering physics), and technical optimization so the simulator runs smoothly on any standard web browser without requiring heavy installations.
